A_drm_visibility.question: Does any unprivileged source enumerate card1 and renderD129 clients?

oracles_tried.detail: enumerates only PIDs whose fd dir is readable to uid 1000
available only where the fd is readable; gave client-id 71 / pdev 0000:01:00.0 for Xwayland
83 attributes enumerated per card; NONE is a client/pasid/fd counter
resource0 is mode 0600 root:root and is NOT a directory; the DRM 'clients' debugfs-style file is not exposed here
debugfs is mounted (type debugfs) but /sys/kernel/debug is drwx------ root:root
read returns empty; not a client oracle
returns 0 / unit not resolved by that name

A_drm_visibility.conclusion: Every DRM client-enumeration path outside /proc requires root. No unprivileged substitute exists on this host.

aggregate_allocation_evidence.question: Can unattributed memory prove or disprove an unseen client?
aggregate_allocation_evidence.interpretation: Xwayland accounts 2184 KiB GTT + 136 KiB VRAM. Aggregate VRAM in use is 5439488 B (~5308 KiB) and aggregate GTT is 12226560 B (~11940 KiB), so a substantial part of the allocation is NOT attributed to any observed client.
aggregate_allocation_evidence.what_this_proves: SUPPORTED — memory is allocated on the RX550 beyond what the single observed client accounts for.
aggregate_allocation_evidence.what_this_does_NOT_prove: UNKNOWN — aggregate counters carry no per-client attribution. The unattributed remainder is consistent with a privileged or unreadable client (kwin_wayland is the obvious candidate) but does NOT demonstrate one. Absence of per-client counters means this evidence can neither confirm nor exclude.
aggregate_allocation_evidence.classification: SUPPORTED (existence of unattributed allocation) / UNKNOWN (its owner)
aggregate_allocation_evidence.explicitly_not_inferred: The unattributed VRAM/GTT is NOT attributed to kwin_wayland. Attributing it would be exactly the inference the task forbids.

B_kwin_1825.question: Can kwin_wayland's relationship to 0000:01:00.0 be established unprivileged?

capability_decoding.significance: Proves a privileged origin: the process is uid 1000 but retains a capability a normal user process cannot hold. It is NOT a DRM capability.
capability_decoding.does_not_explain_denial: CAP_SYS_NICE does not itself gate /proc/<pid>/fd. The denial mechanism is not identified. Yama ptrace_scope=0 is NOT the cause.

parent_exploration.significance: The wrapper holds no DRM node. The FDs it passes to kwin (--wayland-fd 7, --xwayland-fd 8/9) are Wayland/X11 sockets, not DRM nodes. The DRM fd, if any, is opened by kwin_wayland itself and is unobservable.

B_kwin_1825.explicitly_not_inferred: kwin_wayland is the compositor of the active session, and the project's HOST-A evidence recorded it holding card1 and renderD129. NONE of that is transferred. Being the compositor does not demonstrate use of the RX550: the host has an Intel HD 4600 that owns the display connectors (card1-DVI-D-1, card1-HDMI-A-2 connector names are on card0). Its relationship to 0000:01:00.0 is not demonstrable without reading its fd table.

unprivileged_oracles_for_root_clients.detail: resolves some units but not a client list, and returned 0 for kwin_wayland.service

C_root_coverage.conclusion: No unprivileged source enumerates DRM clients held by root-owned processes. The barrier is structural, not a matter of trying harder.

D_namespace_coverage.observation: Of 283 PIDs, 215 have an unreadable /proc/<pid>/fd: 199 root-owned, 5 uid-1000 (sd-pam, kwin_wayland, polkit-kde-auth, ssh-agent, fusermount3), and 11 belonging to other uids.
D_namespace_coverage.uid1000_restricted_case: kwin_wayland (1825) is uid 1000 yet its fd, maps, io, cwd, root and all 7 namespace links are denied, while its parent (1817, same uid) is fully readable. The differentiator was not identified: not Yama (ptrace_scope=0), not seccomp (0), not NoNewPrivs (0). No bypass was attempted.

closure_routes.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: /proc/<pid>/fd + fdinfo for every process holding a RX550 DRM node, including uid 0 and including kwin_wayland
closure_routes.WHY_CURRENT_ACCESS_CANNOT_OBTAIN_IT: Kernel gates those paths on privilege; uid 1000 without CAP_SYS_PTRACE-equivalent cannot read them. ptrace_scope=0 does not help because the restriction is not Yama.
closure_routes.MINIMAL_NEXT_ACTION: A single privileged READ-ONLY collection run, equivalent to the project's own privileged_read_collector.py, as a separately authorized step
closure_routes.RISK: LOW for the collection itself (read-only); it does NOT authorise C1 or isolation

closure_routes.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Writer attribution for governor, IRQ affinity, scheduler, read-ahead, storage on the RX550 and the root filesystem during a measurement window
closure_routes.WHY_CURRENT_ACCESS_CANNOT_OBTAIN_IT: Requires /proc/<pid>/fd of root agents and /sys/kernel/debug or per-CPU irq affinity reads; no unprivileged equivalent
closure_routes.MINIMAL_NEXT_ACTION: Documented as a separate read-only audit; NOT executed here

closure_routes.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A validated, independent recovery path (TTY/console/session) and a verified restore, before any isolation could ever be considered
closure_routes.WHY_CURRENT_ACCESS_CANNOT_OBTAIN_IT: Requires runtime execution; C1 execution is prohibited and PREVIOUS_RECOVERY=FAIL on HOST-A

conclusion.barriers_newly_quantified: The kwin_wayland denial is NOT Yama, NOT seccomp, NOT NoNewPrivs; the mechanism was not identified. 5 uid-1000 processes are affected, not 1.
conclusion.conditions_that_new_evidence_did_satisfy: NONE. This stage produced no condition change; it produced a documented proof that the remaining conditions are unreachable without privilege.
conclusion.absence_not_converted: The absence of visible renderD129 clients and the absence of Kalm were NOT converted into evidence of absence or into ownership FULL.
